name: Sidi Barrani Jass
description: Swiss Jass variant for four players in fixed partnerships. Each deal starts with an auction to set trump (or Obenabe/Undenufe) and the point target the bidders must make. Play is anticlockwise; declarer leads first. Points from tricks, last trick, Weis and Stöck; first team to 2000 wins.
deck: 36 cards (Jass pack; Swiss or French suits)

history.origins: Based on Schieber Jass; originated in Swiss armed forces mid-20th century; popular in Central Switzerland and Swiss overseas communities.
timeline: Mid-20th century: Originated in Swiss armed forces; derived from Schieber Jass. Popular in Central Switzerland and Swiss overseas communities.
history.cultural: Played in fixed partnerships; fashionable in Central Switzerland and among Swiss expatriates (e.g. South America).
history.evolution: Auction for contract and point target distinguishes it from Schieber; Obenabe and Undenufe no-trump options.

setup.players: Four players in fixed partnerships, partners opposite.
setup.deck: 36-card pack (Swiss-German bells, shields, acorns, roses; or French hearts, diamonds, spades, clubs).
setup.dealing: First dealer random. Dealer shuffles, left player cuts. Deal all 36 cards anticlockwise in batches of 3, so each player receives 9 cards. Deal rotates right after each hand.

rules.objective: Bid a contract (trump or Obenabe/Undenufe plus point target). Make at least that many card points in tricks (plus last trick and optional Weis/Stöck). First team to reach 2000 or more points wins; if the losing team has under 1000 it is a double game.
rules.gameplay: After the deal, auction determines trump and point target (40–257). Declarer leads to the first trick. Follow suit or trump; no undertrump unless only trumps in hand. Trick winner leads next. Weis may be declared when playing to the first trick. Score tricks, last trick (5), Weis and Stöck; add bid value to declarers if made, else to opponents.
keyRules: Follow suit when possible; may trump on non-trump lead. No undertrump unless hand is all trumps. Trump Under (Puur) and Nine are highest; 157 points in pack plus 5 for last trick; Match (all nine tricks) scores 257.
Weis declared when playing to first trick; highest Weis combination wins for the team. Stöck (K+O of trumps) claimed after both cards seen.
Auction: bid number (40–257) and denomination (suit or Obenabe or Undenufe). Double by opponent ends auction and doubles stakes.

strategy.basic: Hold the trump Under (Puur); bid a shorter suit with the Under than a long suit without it. Lead to give partner information.
strategy.intermediate: Opening 40/60/80/100 of a suit can guarantee the Under; partner raises with confidence. Compete in Undenufe when opponents have high cards. Sacrifice bids when opponents are likely to make their contract.
strategy.advanced: Cross-ruff to establish long suits; discard shows suit you do not want led. Towards game end, double or outbid when opponents would otherwise reach 2000.
tips: Ask to see partner's Weis in Obenabe/Undenufe to learn which suit to lead.
Do not pass too quickly after a bid; partner may wish to double.

scoring.description: Card points in tricks (157 total), 5 for last trick, 100 for Match (all nine tricks). Weis and Stöck add extra. Bid value (×2 if doubled) added to declarers if contract made, else to opponents. First team to 2000 wins; loser under 1000 = double game.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 2000 or more points wins. If both reach 2000+ in the same deal, play one more deal to break the tie. If the losing team has less than 1000, the winners win a double game.
